review: 1:2–1:3 כִּי נָשָׂאתָ עֲוֺנֵנוּ / וּבְךָ הַפְּדוּת — Isaiah 53:6 (יְהוָה הִפְגִּיעַ בּוֹ אֵת עֲוֺן כֻּלָּנוּ); the Arabic إِذْ حَمَلْتَ إِثْمَنَا is that verse, and נָשָׂאתָ is its verb.
2:2 וּרְצוֹן אֵל הוּשְׁלַם — 'God's pleasure was completed'; the Arabic رِضَا اللهِ اكْتَمَل is the same, and the passive הוּשְׁלַם keeps the divine subject implicit.
2:4 וְהַבְטָחוֹת עוֹלָם — 'and promises of old/eternity'; the Arabic مَوَاعِيدُ الْأَزَل is 'promises of eternity', and עוֹלָם in construct covers both 'ancient' and 'everlasting'.
3:2 הַמָּצָב הַטּוֹב — 'the good standing', for أَحْسَنُ حَال; מָצָב is post-biblical for 'state', but the line needs a noun where a clause would not fit.
4:2 מְקוֹר שִׂמְחַת לֵב — Psalm 4:8 (שִׂמְחָה בְלִבִּי); the Arabic نَبْعُ أَفْرَاحِ الْقُلُوب is a construct chain, and Hebrew keeps the singular heart as the psalm does.
